title: Regulations — Chiang Mai Thailand by UTMB
publisher: UTMB World Series / HOKA Chiang Mai Thailand by UTMB
claims: The runner's commitment requires the ability to confront, without outside assistance, changing climatic conditions that could be very difficult at altitude, including night, wind, cold, fog, rain or snow.
The regulations require each runner to carry all mandatory equipment for the whole race, in a pack that is tagged at bib collection and can be checked at any time.
Aid stations provide still water and sports/electrolyte drink for refilling bottles and hydration packs; runners must leave each station with enough food and drink to reach the next one.

For the 100M, 100K and 50K races, one personal assistant is allowed at certain aid stations, in a reserved area and at the discretion of the team leader, and may hand over only one bag of up to 30 litres.
Runners must stay on the marked path, even when they sleep, and are recommended to use the 'sleep bib' supplied by the organisation if they nap on the route.

Medical, paramedical, first-aid and guide staff may remove a participant deemed unable to continue, require the use of mandatory equipment, evacuate runners in danger and refer them to a care facility.
A runner whose condition justifies an intravenous drip must withdraw from the race compulsorily.

The regulations state that a medical centre is available at 'the Betong Mongkolrit Tunnel (Start/Finish)'; no such tunnel exists at the Doi Inthanon National Park Headquarters used as the start and finish of PAGODA 50.
Runners must leave a checkpoint or aid station before its cut-off time whatever their time of arrival, and new cut-off times in exceptional conditions are announced by SMS, text message or Facebook.
A runner wishing to withdraw must do so at a checkpoint, or reach the nearest checkpoint if already between two checkpoints, and must inform the person responsible or the command centre.
The regulations state that runners will have rest areas at some aid stations, with camp beds and blankets.
The regulations state that no disposable dishes are distributed at check points or aid stations and that runners should bring their own utensils.
The regulations state that trekking poles, if used, must be carried for the entire race and are not allowed in spare bags.
The regulations state that earphones must be removed when crossing roads and at checkpoints or when passing safety team members.
The regulations state that there are several medical stations along the route, directly linked to the command centre, with medical staff at the command centre during events.
The regulations list four ways to call for help: going to a medical station, calling the command centre, asking another runner to call, or using the SOS function in the LiveRun app.
The regulations list age categories from 16-17 to 85+ separately for men and women.
There is no claim in this source about the number of medical stations, ambulance response time, or hospital transfer time.
